title: Diagnosing a saturated database connection pool
content: When database-primary reports a high connection-pool utilization, check for long-running transactions with `SHOW PROCESSLIST` and kill any query running longer than 60s. Verify the application-side pool size matches the documented capacity plan. If utilization stays above 90% after killing stale queries, scale up the read-replica pool before restarting the primary.

title: Restarting a degraded service safely
content: Drain traffic from the instance via the load balancer, wait for in-flight requests to complete (max 30s), then restart the process. Confirm health checks pass for at least 2 minutes before re-adding the instance to rotation. Never restart more than one instance at a time in a cluster smaller than 3 nodes.

title: Incident severity definitions
content: critical: full outage or data loss affecting all customers. high: major functionality broken for a significant subset of customers. medium: degraded performance or a broken non-critical feature. low: cosmetic issue or a workaround exists.

title: auth-service outage response
content: If auth-service is down, immediately check the identity-provider upstream status page. Most outages are caused by an expired signing certificate — check cert expiry with `openssl x509 -enddate` against the configured JWKS endpoint. If the cert is valid, roll back the last deploy and open a critical incident.

title: payment-api elevated latency runbook
content: Elevated checkout latency is most commonly caused by the fraud-scoring service timing out. Check its p99 latency dashboard first. If fraud-scoring is healthy, check database-primary connection pool saturation, since payment-api shares the primary with the order service.

title: On-call escalation policy
content: Page the primary on-call engineer for any high or critical severity incident. If there is no acknowledgment within 10 minutes, escalate to the secondary on-call, then to the engineering manager. Escalate directly to the manager for any incident involving customer data exposure.

title: Safe rollback procedure
content: Identify the last known-good release tag from the deployment dashboard. Roll back via the standard deploy pipeline (never `kubectl edit` directly). Announce the rollback in the incident channel and monitor error rates for 15 minutes before closing the incident.

title: Cache invalidation checklist
content: Stale cache entries after a schema migration should be cleared via the `cache-service` admin endpoint's `/flush?namespace=` route, never a full flush in production. Confirm the namespace before flushing to avoid a cold-cache stampede on unrelated services.

title: Rate limiting and backpressure
content: search-api enforces a token-bucket rate limit of 200 req/s per API key. A burst of 429s from a single key usually indicates a misbehaving batch job, not an outage — check the caller's request pattern before treating it as an incident.

title: TLS certificate renewal
content: Certificates are auto-renewed 30 days before expiry via the ACME client. If auto-renewal fails, check the ACME client logs for DNS-01 challenge failures, then renew manually with the documented `certbot renew --manual` procedure and redeploy the ingress.

title: Log aggregation and search tips
content: Use the `service:<name> AND level:error` query in the log aggregator to scope investigation quickly. Correlate by `trace_id` across services rather than timestamp alone, since clocks can drift by a few seconds between hosts.

title: Notification delivery failures
content: If customer-facing notifications are delayed, check the notification-service outbound queue depth first. A growing queue with a healthy consumer count usually means a downstream provider (email/SMS) is throttling — check their status page before escalating internally.

title: When to open an incident vs. a ticket
content: Open an incident (not just a ticket) whenever customer-facing functionality is degraded or down, or when a security-relevant event is detected. Internal-only issues with no customer impact should be filed as a ticket instead, even if urgent.
